aiOverview.content: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT, concluding a 10-day trip around the moon. Full video coverage of the reentry and splashdown, including the capsule's parachute deployment, is available on PBS, WBAL-TV, and the NASA YouTube channel.Key Aspects of the Artemis II Splashdown:Location: The Orion capsule landed west of San Diego.Crew: Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen returned safely.Footage Highlights: Videos show the fiery reentry, the deployment of parachutes, and the final splashdown into the Pacific.Recovery: A joint NASA and U.S. military team was on-site to retrieve the capsule and crew.You can view the full, recorded video of the splashdown on the WBAL-TV site and see expert commentary from PBS. The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT, concluding a 10-day trip around the moon. Full video coverage of the reentry and splashdown, including the capsule's parachute deployment, is available on PBS, WBAL-TV, and the NASA YouTube channel. PBS WBAL-TV NASA YouTube channel Key Aspects of the Artemis II Splashdown: Location: The Orion capsule landed west of San Diego. Crew: Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen returned safely. Footage Highlights: Videos show the fiery reentry, the deployment of parachutes, and the final splashdown into the Pacific. Recovery: A joint NASA and U.S. military team was on-site to retrieve the capsule and crew.
